en: The Jātaka:
The Ninth Chapter, The Section on Vultures (Gijjhavagga)
12. The Daddara Jātaka:
“He who ate your two innocent sons, even though you had given him their food—”
“Set your fang upon him;
let him not escape you alive!
“A man is full of cruelty,” [he replied].
Like a nurse’s garment soiled [with blood],
I do not see any spot where I might set down my fang.
To a person who is ungrateful and always looking for faults,
even if one were to give the entire earth, [it would not be enough].
“Nor did I please him. “Why is it,
Subāhu, that you have returned in such a hurried manner together with the young brahmin?”
"What is the purpose here for you?
Being asked, tell me this matter.
"Your friend Daddara, who is of noble character—"
Today I fear for his life;
having heard of the spheres of action of that man,
I do not consider Daddara to be safe today.
“What spheres of action would he have,
by virtue of a man’s attainment of livelihood? Or what declaration,
having heard it from a man, [would he accept]?”
“You suspect that the Daddara was killed by the young brahmin.
“The Kaliṅgas have been subdued, trade has been carried out,
the Vettavatī region has been traversed, and even the path of thorns has been traveled.”
Actors, together with their wives,
even fought with sticks in the midst of the assembly;
they were bound by the measure of a *kulīka* and a measured *māḷhaka*.
The dice are won, self-restraint has been transcended;
at the dead of night, the ancient debt is paid,
for the hands have been burned by the receiving of alms.
These would be his spheres of action for a man, through the accomplishment of his livelihood;
just as this mass of hair is seen here.
“The cows have been killed; what then of Daddara?
Thus ends the twelfth Jātaka, the Daddara-jātaka.
The Ninth Chapter (Navaka-nipāta) is concluded.
Its summary verse:
Varagijjha, Samajjana, Haṃsavara,
Nidhi, Savhaya, Hārita, and Pāṭalika.
How can there be endurance for one who is subject to old age and death?
Therefore, there is fear for one who gazes upon the twelve [links of dependent origination].
